I will think about this the way I always do — what worked last year, what my neighbors do, and how much money I can spend.

My main land is the wheat-maize rotation, that is 18 mu. I plant wheat in October, then drill maize straight into the stubble in June. That is what everybody around here does, no need to plough between them — saves diesel and time. The cotton I keep on a 2 mu plot near the road, it has done alright there for many years. The peanut, millet, and mung bean are small patches, mostly for the house and to give some land a rest from grain.

For fertilizer I buy 复合肥 (compound) at planting and 尿素 (urea) for topdress. I always put plenty — the seed shop man and my neighbors all say more nitrogen, more grain. If I save 50 yuan and lose 50 kg of wheat, I lose much more. So I do not save on fertilizer. On wheat I spread two bags of compound per mu before planting and one bag of urea at jointing — that comes to about 28 kg nitrogen per mu. On maize the same idea, a bit less because the soil already had wheat fertilizer.

Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm and aphids come every year, I spray four or five times. Peanut and mung bean I do not put much nitrogen, my father always said beans make their own.

I have a well so I water the wheat two or three times — before winter, at green-up, and at heading if it is dry. Maize usually one watering at tasseling, the summer rain does the rest.
